direct_answer: Yes. BASF states that it has developed a climate change mitigation transition plan to achieve its climate protection targets (Scope 1+2: -25% by 2030 vs. 2018; net-zero GHG emissions by 2050) and describes key levers (renewable energy, operational excellence, low-emission steam generation) [Source 1]. BASF also states that its Scope 1+2 target is compatible with limiting global warming to 1.5°C, based on the International Energy Agency (IEA) “Net Zero by 2050” emission reduction pathways [Source 1]. The retrieved passages do not provide sufficient evidence to conclude that BASF’s full transition plan (beyond the stated Scope 1+2 target) is aligned with 1.5°C across all relevant scopes (e.g., Scope 3), as BASF notes that the IEA study does not provide a basis for deriving an emissions reduction pathway for its raw materials-related Scope 3.1 emissions [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: Evidence confirms existence of a transition plan and an explicit 1.5°C-compatibility statement for the Scope 1+2 target, including the referenced framework (IEA Net Zero by 2050 pathways) [Source 1]. However, the retrieved passages do not include the ESRS E1-4 details needed to fully substantiate 1.5°C alignment (e.g., whether targets are science-based, methodology details beyond the IEA reference, scenarios for targets, external assurance) and explicitly indicate a limitation for Scope 3.1 pathway derivation [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Whether BASF’s GHG targets are formally science-based (e.g., validated by SBTi) and the specific framework/methodology used for target-setting beyond referencing IEA pathways for Scope 1+2 [Source 1, Source 14].
Underlying climate and policy scenarios used specifically to set/assess the GHG reduction targets (as opposed to general scenario analysis for transition risks) [Source 2].
Whether BASF’s GHG targets and/or transition plan have been externally assured [Source 1].
Clear evidence that the transition plan is 1.5°C-aligned across all material emissions scopes, including Scope 3 (BASF indicates no IEA pathway basis for Scope 3.1) [Source 1].
key_findings: BASF reports having developed a climate change mitigation transition plan to achieve its climate protection targets [Source 1].
BASF’s Scope 1+2 target is to reduce emissions 25% by 2030 vs. 2018 and achieve net-zero GHG emissions by 2050 [Source 1].
BASF states its Scope 1+2 target is compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C, referencing IEA “Net Zero by 2050” pathways [Source 1].

BASF set a Scope 3.1 (raw materials-related) target in 2023 (15% reduction by 2030 vs. 2022, intensity vs purchasing volume), but notes the IEA study does not provide a basis for deriving a reduction pathway for these emissions [Source 1].
